The weight W of the ladder acts through the centre of gravity G. Forces also act on the ladder at
P and at Q. These forces are P and Q respectively.
Which vector triangle represents the forces on the ladder?

hints: Notice $W$ must be a long arrow acting vertically downward through G, so reject any triangle where $W$ points upward.
Recall both contacts are rough, so $P$ at the wall and $Q$ at the ground each have normal plus friction components and are tilted away from the normal.
Connect equilibrium $P + Q + W = 0$ to head-to-tail addition: the three arrows must join to form a closed triangle with consistent direction around the loop.
walkthrough: Identify the forces: $W$ acts vertically downward at G, $P$ is the resultant contact force at the top against the rough wall, and $Q$ is the resultant contact force at the bottom on rough ground.
State the equilibrium rule for coplanar forces: the vector sum must be zero, so when placed head-to-tail $P$, $Q$ and $W$ must form a closed triangle.
Check direction of $W$: it must point straight down, which leaves only the triangles where the $W$ arrow points downward.
Check tilt of $P$ and $Q$: because friction acts, neither contact force is purely horizontal or vertical, so both $P$ and $Q$ sides must be slanted.
Check head-to-tail closure: place $W$ down, then $Q$ up and to the right from the end of $W$, then $P$ back to the start, giving a consistent clockwise loop with no gap. This is option A.

A.explanation: Closed triangle with $W$ vertically down and $P$ and $Q$ angled by friction gives $P + Q + W = 0$ for equilibrium.

B.explanation: The $P$ arrow is reversed, which would make the three vectors fail to follow head-to-tail closure in the correct directions.

C.explanation: The $P$ arrow points the wrong way along its side, so the head-to-tail loop does not give zero resultant.

D.explanation: Both $W$ and $Q$ are drawn vertically but on opposite sides, so $W$ is shown acting upward instead of downward.
